## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

The *Dutiyanibbānapaṭisaṁyutta Sutta* (Ud 8.2, PTS Ud 80) is the second discourse in the eighth chapter of the *Udāna* [SuttaCentral]. The text concerns the realization and seeing of extinguishment (*nibbāna*) [SuttaCentral]. Modern translations listed on SuttaCentral include eighteen versions across fifteen languages, among them an English translation by Bhikkhu Sujato [SuttaCentral].

SuttaCentral identifies resembling parallels in the verse collections of the northern Buddhist traditions, specifically within the Nirvāṇa chapter (*Nirvāṇavarga*) of the Sanskrit *Udānavarga* (UV 26; UVS 26), the Tibetan translation (Uv Kg 26), and related Chinese collections such as the *Faju jing* (T 210.36), T 212.27, and T 213.26 [SuttaCentral].

Within the Pali canon, DharmaNexus records twenty instances of text reuse across six texts [DharmaNexus]. Most prominently, the discourse shares extensive segments (§0.1–2.1) with the surrounding discourses on *nibbāna* in the same chapter of the *Udāna*: the *Paṭhamanibbānapaṭisaṁyutta Sutta* (Ud 8.1), *Tatiyanibbānapaṭisaṁyutta Sutta* (Ud 8.3), and *Catutthanibbānapaṭisaṁyutta Sutta* (Ud 8.4) [DharmaNexus]. In addition, DharmaNexus aligns passages (§1.3–2.1) with discourses in the *Māra Saṁyutta* (SN 4) and the *Vaṅgīsa Saṁyutta* (SN 8), as well as sharing text (§1.2–1.3) with the *Catukkanipāta* of the *Aṅguttara Nikāya* (AN 4) [DharmaNexus].

*No discussion of this text was found in the reference-literature corpus; the overview relies on SuttaCentral and DharmaNexus data.*
